subject: Re: Log handoff manifest & time-gated retention proposal

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Bulk audit extract requirements and manifest

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the RFP materials earlier this week. Our security and e-discovery teams have a few follow-ups specific to audit/log handoffs:

- We need a clear manifest schema that accompanies bulk extracts (fields, ordering, checksums, signature).
- Can you support time-gated slices (e.g., deliver a 30–90 day rolling slice per request) vs full archive pulls?
- What's your retention tiering (default retention windows, long-term retention options up to 7+ years)?
- Export formats: JSONL, CSV, Parquet — which are supported as first-class? Any per-export size limits?
- Tamper-evidence: do exports include signed manifests or WORM retention options?
- We also need an SLA for export completion (e.g., X TB completed within Y business days) and a proposed cost model for large bulk pulls.

We would like a written proposal describing the manifest, the timegate concept, snapshot cadence (full vs incremental), encryption-at-rest/in-transit details, and a sample deliverable.

Can you and your team respond by EOD Friday? If feasible, please include a small sample export we can inspect.

Thanks,
Jill Anders
Head of Security Programs
Northbridge Financial

Hi Jill —

Appreciate the clear list. We're happy to provide a detailed proposal and a sample export. Quick summary / commitment:

- We'll supply a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums + signer metadata) that lists every object in the bundle and a small schema doc.
- Time-gated slices are supported. We can produce ad-hoc slices (30/90/365 days) and a custom timegate window you specify.
- Supported formats: JSONL (primary), CSV (flat records), Parquet (columnar for large analytical loads).
- Snapshot cadence: daily incremental diffs, weekly full snapshots by default (configurable).
- Export SLA: propose baseline 3 business days for bundles < 5 TB; escalation SLA and expedited options available at commit.

Aditya and Marissa are copied and will include technical and delivery specifics. We'll attach a sample manifest and a small sample bundle for you to inspect.

I'll follow up with a scheduling link so we can review the sample together.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Jill Anders <jill.anders@northbridge.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Bulk audit extract requirements and manifest

Hi all —

Below are the recommended deliverable details and the technical design we propose. This is intentionally prescriptive so your e-discovery team can validate against tooling.

1) Manifest (proposed-manifest-v1.csv) — one CSV per bundle with header and the following columns (CSV, UTF-8):
   - object_key (string) — full path in the bundle or S3 key
   - record_type (enum) — audit_event | access_log | system_trace | config_change
   - event_timestamp (ISO8601)
   - record_id (UUID)
   - sequence_number (long) — incremental within stream
   - file_offset (int) — byte offset if packed inside a blob
   - object_size_bytes (int)
   - sha256_checksum (hex)
   - crc32c (optional)
   - signer_identity (string) — subject DN of the signing key
   - signature (base64) — manifest signature (see below)

2) Timegate semantics — we define a timegate as a pair (start_ts, end_ts). Exports can be:
   - ad-hoc slice: arbitrary start/end you request
   - rolling window presets: 30d, 90d, 365d
   - bucketed slices: by day/week/month for stream rehydration

3) Snapshot cadence & packaging — default pattern: daily incremental diffs (JSONL delta files) plus weekly full snapshots.
   - Deltas are append-only JSONL files named by stream and date.
   - Weekly full is a compressed archive (tar.gz) containing the week's deltas plus index files.

4) Tamper-evidence & signing —
   - Manifests are signed with an HSM-backed key (RSA-4096 or ECDSA-P521 by request).
   - Each object includes SHA256. The manifest signature covers the manifest CSV bytes and is verifiable independently.
   - Optional WORM retention (S3 Object Lock) can be applied per-customer export for legal hold windows.

5) Storage & transfer —
   - Delivery options: S3 (pre-signed URL or cross-account replication), HTTPS streaming (multipart), or customer-provided storage connector.
   - Encryption in transit: TLS1.2+; at rest: SSE-KMS by default; customer-managed KMS available.

6) Integrity & verification —
   - Checksums (sha256) in manifest + object metadata; we can provide a verification tool (small Python script) as part of the sample bundle.

7) SLAs & sizing guidance —
   - Baseline: 3 business days for <5TB, 7 business days for 5–50TB. Expedited windows available for add-on.

8) Cost model suggestion —
   - Per-GB exported + per-bundle processing fee + optional expedited premium. We'll provide a quote once we know expected volumes and cadence.

I've attached a short sample export structure (sample-export-structure.txt) and a draft manifest CSV. Marcus, any notes on long-term retention/archival tiers?

-- Aditya
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very thorough and the manifest fields look good. A couple of follow-ups:

- We want to confirm long-term retention options. Our default request is: 365 days active + 6 years archived (immutably stored). Will you commit to offering an archival tier with WORM for 6 years?
- For the SLA, can you provide an expedited 24–48 hour option for emergency legal pulls? What would the premium look like?
- We'd like to schedule a test export for next Wednesday (Nov 24) in your staging environment — a small 20 GB bundle with the signature manifest and verification script.

Also please include a simple cost estimate (ballpark) for: one-off 50 TB pull vs ongoing monthly 2 TB exports.

Regards,
Jill

Jill —

We can confirm the following and next steps:

- Archival tier: yes — we support an archival option with S3 Object Lock (governance or compliance mode) for up to 7 years. We'll provide the retention lock metadata in the manifest and include a WORM attestation.
- Expedited SLA: we offer a 24–48 hour emergency export option subject to resource scheduling; pricing is a function of TB + priority fee. We'll provide a redline to the contract with a predefined emergency pull addendum if needed.
- Test export: Nov 24 works for staging. We'll provision a staging bucket and share cross-account access. Expect an invite for a 30-minute verification call.
- Cost ballpark (preliminary):
   - One-off 50 TB pull: processing + egress estimate $9,000–$14,000 (depends on compression factor and transfer method).
   - Ongoing monthly 2 TB exports: ~$800/month (processing + egress), can be lowered with committed monthly retainer.

Next actions:
  1) I'll send a HubSpot deal link and DocuSign addendum for the archival/WORM option.
  2) Aditya will deliver the sample bundle and verification script to the staging bucket by EOD Monday (Nov 23).
  3) Marissa will coordinate procurement/PO and provide a pricing workbook.

Attachments: proposed-manifest-v1.csv, sample-export-structure.txt, s3-delivery-playbook.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the test run.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
